constraints.why: the nanobody itself must be confidently predicted, or nothing measured on its paratope means anything
the fold has to survive the fusion; past about 2 A the core has moved
a linker cut no more at the site than in circulation unmasks in transit, which is the failure the design exists to prevent
a linker a protease cannot reach is not cleavable at any sequence

front_order: maximin on the normalised objectives: ordered by the weakest of the three. The front itself is a set; this is a stated rule applied to it, not a property of it.
normalisation: min-max within the feasible set, so the three scales are comparable. Not a calibration against measured quantities, which do not exist for these scores.
note: hard constraints first, then the nondominated set, then maximin on the normalised objectives. No weights are applied at any step, and the ordering is a stated rule rather than a property of the front.

objective_basis.cleavability: predicted human-MMP selectivity times structural reach of the linker; not a cleavage rate, and not specificity for a snake venom metalloproteinase
objective_basis.feasibility: a heuristic combination of predicted fold confidence, nanobody preservation, exposed hydrophobic surface and measured disulfide pairing
objective_basis.surface_occlusion: paratope surface lost in the folded construct. It is named for what it measures: the controls show it does not separate designed masks from scrambled or inert ones, so it is not a masking score and a front built on it is not a list of masked nanobodies
